ask.en: You want to clean the bathroom. What is safe?

text.en: Use one cleaner at a time. Never mix bleach with other cleaners.

why.en: Yes! Mixing bleach with other cleaners can make a poison gas.

text.en: Mix bleach and another cleaner so it is extra strong.

why.en: Stronger is not safer. Mixing cleaners can make poison gas.

text.en: Pour bleach in, then add another cleaner after.

why.en: The order does not matter. Mixing them can still make poison gas.

tip.en: Never mix bleach with other cleaners.

ask.en: A cleaner is in an old juice bottle. What should happen?

text.en: Keep products in their own labelled bottles.

why.en: Yes! The label tells everyone what is inside and how to stay safe.

text.en: Leave it in the juice bottle. It is easier to carry.

why.en: Someone might think it is juice and drink it. Always keep the original bottle.

text.en: Draw a smiley on the bottle so everyone knows.

why.en: A smiley does not tell anyone what is inside. Keep the original label.

tip.en: Keep products in their original labelled bottles.

ask.en: Your baby sister crawls everywhere. Where do the cleaners go?

text.en: High up, or in a cupboard that is locked.

why.en: Yes! Little kids touch and taste everything, so keep products out of their reach.

text.en: On the floor under the sink.

why.en: A crawling baby can reach the floor easily. Store products up high or locked away.

text.en: In the bathroom, next to the toys.

why.en: Products must never be near toys. Store them high or locked away.

tip.en: Store products high or locked away from little siblings.
